articles.title: “Just doing my part over here”: Patrick Mahomes’ wife Brittany Mahomes makes an emotional update about his career and their growing family
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes, the Kansas City Chiefs’ quarterback, has bounced back well in the ongoing season after the severe injuries he sustained in the last
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes, the Kansas City Chiefs’ quarterback, has bounced back well in the ongoing season after the severe injuries he sustained in the last season. While Patrick Mahomes has put his mind on the field, he is also set to become a father food the fourth time. Amid this, his wife Brittany Mahomes has made another heartfelt update.Patrick Mahomes' wife Brittany Mahomes makes an emotional post about his career and their fourth babyA few hours ago, Patrick Mahomes' wife Brittany Mahomes took to her social media to share a post made by Complex Sports about their fourth child.The post read as, “Every time Brittany Mahomes has been pregnant during an NFL season, Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs have reached the Super Bowl. 🏆”The post also added, “With the recent announcement of their fourth child on the way, fans are already pointing to the streak as a hopeful sign for another Super Bowl run.”The Kansas City Current co-owner Brittany Mahomes posted this on her social media with a caption that read as, “Glad someone finally figured this out. Just doing my part over here…”While many fans have found the post pretty funny, others have been emotional concerning how Patrick Mahomes and his wife have built a beautiful family in the last few years.Both Patrick Mahomes and his wife, Brittany Mahomes, have remained present parents to their three children, Sterling, Bronze and Golden Raye.While the top quarterback has been extremely busy with his career in the last few years, he has often expressed gratitude to his wife, Brittany Mahomes, for managing their home when he is away working.Brittany Mahomes has continued to focus on her career as she stands by Patrick Mahomes’ sideAs Brittany Mahomes is all set to be a mother to four children in the next few months, she has not let motherhood get in the way of her career.Ever since Patrick Mahomes became one of the most popular players in the league, Brittany Mahomes has turned into a popular social media investor, a successful investor and an entrepreneur.Brittany Mahomes has continued to work with several brands as she remains a pretty strategic investor in various emerging brands.For now, the focus remains on the top quarterback’s performance as he is all set to face the Atlanta Falcons after the win against the New York Jets.A few weeks ago, in an interview with CBS Sports, the team’s head coach Andy Reid reflected on how Patrick Mahomes recovered from his severe injuries as he said, “He just goes. He kept playing, he gets his rehab taken care of before and after practice, you know how he is — he’s all in…He’s a great example to all the other guys around him that, ‘I’m gonna do whatever I have to do to get myself on the field,’” Reid continued.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Vikings Wanted Kirk Cousins Trade Before Wentz Struggled, Latest NFL Rumors on Raiders Talks
articles.summary: Despite the conventional wisdom being the Minnesota Vikings pursued the Kirk Cousins trade in direct response to Carson Wentz's performance on Monday Night Football, they actually reached out to the Las Vegas Raiders before their 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
articles.body:
Despite the conventional wisdom being the Minnesota Vikings pursued the Kirk Cousins trade in direct response to Carson Wentz's performance on Monday Night Football, they actually reached out to the Las Vegas Raiders before their 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills.

Per ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , the Vikings' first call to the Raiders about Cousins came a few hours before Monday's kickoff and they "made it clear" they wanted to see how Wentz played before taking things further.

The report also noted Minnesota's initial offer of a fifth-round pick for Cousins was of no interest to the Raiders, but the tide shifted when it was bumped up to a 2027 third-round selection:

Kirk Trade Result of Vikings' 'Desperation'

"It was not a deal the Raiders wanted, nor were looking to make, especially when Minnesota's initial offer was a fifth-round draft pick, according to sources.

"But once the Vikings upped their offer to a third-round pick, the Raiders had discussions about whether the trade made sense, and here's where they landed:

"Not only would they be receiving a third-round pick, but they also would be freeing up $10 million in cash for the 2027 season, as the bonus guarantee owed to Cousins would shift to Minnesota's responsibility. It was not a trade that the Raiders enjoyed making, but it was one they believed would be in the best interests of the organization."

Wentz got the start against Buffalo with Kyler Murray unavailable due to a hamstring injury. He played well when called upon earlier in the season, including throwing for 133 yard and three touchdowns in a 39-22 win over the Green Bay Packers in Week 1.

Things did not go well this time around for Wentz. He finished 8-of-25 for 81 yards with two interceptions against Buffalo's defense.

The Vikings got the deal done with the Raiders shortly before Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET trade deadline by giving up their 2027 third-round seelction.

Even before Wentz's disastrous outing and Murray's injury, there were reasons for the Vikings to explore the quarterback trade market. Murray ranks 26th in QBR and 27th in success rate out of 31 qualified quarterbacks this season.

Cousins has been much better than expected in nine starts with the Raiders. He has thrown for 2,430 yards, 20 touchdowns and completed 64.1 percent of his attempts.

Murray, Wentz and Max Brosmer combined have thrown for 1,286 yards, eight touchdowns, five interceptions and completed 60.9 percent of their attempts.

Adding to the value for Minnesota is Cousins' built-in familiarity with head coach Kevin O'Connell's system from their two seasons together in 2022 and '23. He was also the Vikings quarterback for Justin Jefferson's first four seasons.

Jefferson averaged 98 receptions, 1,475 yards and 7.5 touchdowns per season from 2020 to '23. His numbers have dipped to 73 receptions, 991 yards and 5.3 touchdowns per season without Cousins.

Minnesota's defense has been the best in the NFL this season with 14.6 points allowed per game, so any upgrade at quarterback would have made this team a top-tier Super Bowl contender.

Cousins is more than capable of playing well for the offense to succeed, especially knowing the Vikings defense will more than hold up their end of the bargain.

articles.title: $105 million Pro Bowler could be the missing piece the Cincinnati Bengals need to make a serious playoff push
articles.summary: The Cincinnati Bengals missed an important opportunity to strengthen their secondary before the NFL trade deadline.
articles.body: The Cincinnati Bengals missed an important opportunity to strengthen their secondary before the NFL trade deadline. Their failed attempt to add cornerback help has left a familiar weakness unresolved, and there is still a veteran option available. Four-time Pro Bowler Marshon Lattimore remains without a team after his release from Washington. With Cincinnati preparing for a crucial stretch of the season, bringing in the former New Orleans Saints star could give its defense some much-needed experience and depth. The move would carry some risk, but the potential reward is worth considering.Cincinnati Bengals could find a defensive solution in Marshon LattimoreCincinnati's need for another cornerback has become increasingly difficult to overlook. The Bengals have DJ Turner as a reliable option on the outside, while Dax Hill offers flexibility as both a slot and outside defender. The problem begins when the coaching staff tries to use both players in their preferred roles.If Hill moves inside, the Bengals need another dependable outside corner. If he stays outside, the slot position becomes less settled. Jalen Davis, Josh Newton and DJ Ivey have all been involved in the rotation, but none has provided the consistency Cincinnati needs.That is where Lattimore enters the discussion.Bleacher Report's Moe Moton recently identified Cincinnati and Detroit as two suitable destinations for the veteran cornerback. Moton pointed out that neither team managed to land a cornerback before the deadline.“Some speculated that the Cincinnati Bengals and Detroit Lions would try to trade for cornerbacks before the deadline,” wrote Moton. “Neither team acquired one. Lattimore could be a solid in-season acquisition for either club.”Lattimore has earned nearly $105 million during his 10-year NFL career. He was selected 11th overall by New Orleans in 2017 and won Defensive Rookie of the Year honors. Four Pro Bowl selections followed, establishing him as one of the more respected cornerbacks of his generation.Lattimore's injury history makes the move a calculated riskThere is a reason Lattimore remains available, though. His recent seasons have been interrupted by injuries, and his performances have not always matched the level he showed during his best years in New Orleans.He started seven games in 2022, 10 in 2023 and nine in 2024 before moving to Washington. His time with the Commanders also failed to bring much stability. He appeared in only two games during the 2024 season and nine in 2025 before Washington released him in March 2026. He also suffered an ACL injury in Week 9 of 2025, making his recovery an important factor for any interested team.Cincinnati would need to assess his fitness before making a commitment. Still, the Bengals do not necessarily need Lattimore to return to his Pro Bowl level immediately. A healthy veteran who can handle meaningful snaps would already give the coaching staff more choices.The timing matters, too. Cincinnati faces Pittsburgh in Week 11, a matchup with major AFC North implications. The Bengals have made their intentions clear with an aggressive roster approach this season, but their secondary remains an area that needs attention.Lattimore may not be the complete answer. Yet leaving a clear weakness untouched could prove more costly when the games become more important. For Cincinnati, this is a chance to add experience without giving up another draft pick.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: NFL reassigns 3 officials following nationwide FAA ground stop
articles.summary: The ground stop order was lifted Friday night, but not before it affected games in the NFL and college football this weekend.
articles.body:
The ground stop order issued by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) on Friday has now affected the NFL after having an impact on this weekend's college football games .

On Saturday morning, the NFL announced that several officiating assignments for Week 10 have been adjusted. Officials were reassigned to games that are within driving distance of their hometowns.

Barry Anderson and Duane Heydt, who normally serve as umpires, along with side judge Don Willard, will take on referee duties on Sunday.

Anderson will officiate the Jacksonville Jaguars-Tennessee Titans game in Tennessee; Heydt has been assigned to work the Carolina Panthers-New Orleans Saints game in New Orleans; and Willard will have double-duty first refereeing the Miami Dolphins-Indianapolis Colts game in Indianapolis at 1 p.m. ET before making the trip to Cincinnati for Sunday night's game between the Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers at 8:20 p.m. ET.

"Each of the league's 17 officiating crews have a backup referee identified, and that individual trains throughout the year to work at the referee position should the need arise," the NFL said.

According to The Ringer's Tom Pelissero , another change will see replay duties in the Panthers-Saints game handled by the league's replay center in New York and not an official in the stadium.

The ground stop order was put in place on Friday due to a "temporary telecommunications outage" affecting air traffic control, the FAA announced .

That stop was lifted as of 8:15 p.m. ET Friday, but even with flights allowed to resume, it led to kickoff changes for some college games. Almost all of the Power Four conferences have teams that were prevented from reaching their destinations. Only the ACC has every team already ready to go. One SEC matchup — Ole Miss vs. Oklahoma — was postponed to Sunday .

"It'll be slow," Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy said Friday about the resumption of nationwide air travel.

It's the second nationwide ground stop since 9/11, per ABC News , which noted that this last happened in 2023 . At the time, pilots were unable to access their pre-departure paperwork because the FAA NOTAM (Notice To all Air Missions) system — used to disseminate flight hazards and real-time restrictions to pilots — went down.

articles.title: Mac Jones Trade Demand from 49ers to Vikings Revealed in New NFL Rumors After Kirk Cousins Deal
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers' high asking price reportedly ended the Minnesota Vikings' pursuit of quarterback Mac Jones ahead of the NFL trade deadline this week.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers' high asking price reportedly ended the Minnesota Vikings' pursuit of quarterback Mac Jones ahead of the NFL trade deadline this week.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , the Vikings called the Niners about Jones, but discussions ended when San Francisco asked for a second-round pick and more in exchange for its backup signal-caller.

Instead, the Vikings opted to bring Kirk Cousins back to Minnesota, acquiring him from the Las Vegas Raiders for a third-round pick.

Kirk Trade Result of Vikings' 'Desperation'

Per Schefter and Rapoport, the pre-deadline conversations were not the first time the Vikings and 49ers held talks focused on Jones.

However, 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan reportedly views Jones as a "franchise-caliber quarterback," and the Niners did not want to trade him unless they got an offer that they "had no choice but to accept."

Jones, 28, is in the midst of his second season with the 49ers after stints as a member of the New England Patriots and Jacksonville Jaguars.

While he has not attempted a pass this season due to starting quarterback Brock Purdy staying healthy, Jones played a significant role in San Francisco reaching the playoffs last season.

Jones appeared in 11 games and made eight starts, as Purdy struggled through multiple injuries.

The one-time Pro Bowler went 5-3 in those starts, completing 69.6 percent of his passes for 2,151 yards, 13 touchdowns and six interceptions.

Originally selected 15th overall by the Patriots in the 2021 NFL draft, he did not pan out as a starter in New England, but there is seemingly a strong chance that Jones could get a chance to start somewhere next season provided he opts to leave San Francisco in free agency.

Should that happen, Jones would be following a path similar to Sam Darnold, who spent 2023 as the 49ers' backup before earning Pro Bowl honors with the Vikings in 2024 and leading the Seattle Seahawks to a Super Bowl win in 2025.

With Cousins, Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz all playing on expiring contracts, Jones could very well be an option for Minnesota in free agency this coming offseason.

For now, the Vikings are hoping Cousins' return will breathe new life into an offense that has lagged well behind a defense that ranks first in the NFL in points allowed and second in yards allowed.

At 6-2, Minnesota is just a half-game behind the Chicago Bears for the NFC North lead, and with an improved offense, the Vikings could be Super Bowl contenders.

articles.title: Jets Icon Darrelle Revis Talks Aaron Glenn, Arch Manning, Coaching Interest & More in B/R Interview
articles.summary: As arguably the greatest player in New York Jets franchise history, Hall of Fame cornerback Darrelle Revis has lived through the team's thrilling highs and agonizing heartbreaks.
articles.body:
As arguably the greatest player in New York Jets franchise history, Hall of Fame cornerback Darrelle Revis has lived through the team's thrilling highs and agonizing heartbreaks.

So even with the Jets' 2-7 record entering Sunday's game against the 7-1 Buffalo Bills, Revis can still find reasons for optimism. While highlighting New York's three first-round picks in the 2027 NFL draft, the 41-year-old gave his thoughts on the future of head coach Aaron Glenn, who is 5-21 two years into the job.

"I think it's premature to fire Aaron Glenn. I just think it is," Revis told Bleacher Report. "I think with what we have in the value of the draft picks, I think we need to give him a third year to really hone in… The QB position always solves some of the issues when you got a great quarterback."

The 2027 draft class is expected to be loaded with talented signal-callers, giving the Jets a chance to finally secure their franchise quarterback after years of instability at the position. With prospects such as Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker and Notre Dame's CJ Carr rising up draft boards, Revis weighed in on who he'd like to see under center for New York, as well as what the team should do with its other first-round picks.

"If it's Arch Manning, we love it. He has so much potential," Revis said of the Texas quarterback. "And he comes from a family legacy that knows how to play at a high level of football. So, it's a lot of excitement ahead, I think."

He later added: "I like Leonard Moore, the cornerback from Notre Dame, he's a pretty solid cover corner. We need that back in the secondary, too. Seems like he'll bring a lot of leadership early on, with how he plays at Notre Dame. Coach [Marcus] Freeman is doing a great job developing those young men at Notre Dame."

A shutdown cornerback would surely solve New York's interception problem, as the team has just one pick in 26 games under Glenn. Revis is responsible for one of the greatest cornerback seasons in NFL history, setting a league record with 31 passes defended in 2009, so he knows what it takes to create a successful secondary. The seven-time Pro Bowler gave a thoughtful answer on what the Jets should do to improve their defensive backfield.

"When I played, for me, I've always tried to focus on great study habits. That's one. Attention to detail, especially in the back end of the secondary, only because it's such an uncomfortable position to play. The cornerback position and the safety position. If the ball goes over our head and it's a touchdown, it's an embarrassment," he said. "The fans are going wild about it. So we have to be very focused and have attention to detail in what we're doing and what we're trying to execute as a unit.

"There's a lot of communication on the back end amongst the safeties and the corners to make sure we're on the same page, to play at a very high level, and be playmakers. I think it's about being playmakers and making plays," he continued. "Our job is, we're the last line of defense, and our job is to stop people from making touchdowns. And I think that's the gist of it. And then also playmakers, just make plays in the passing game. If you can get your hands on that ball, we want to turn it over."

With so much insight and expertise, Revis has what it takes to be a successful defensive backs coach in the NFL. While he said he's satisfied with his current life in real estate business ventures and other investments, he clearly has a passion for teaching the tidbits that made him so successful in the league, and he revealed whether he would be willing to lend a hand to his old franchise.

"I'm here, I can be available. It has to be the right situation, obviously. But I'm here," Revis said when asked if he would be interested in a job as a DB coach. "The Jets, if they want to call and have a conversation, I'm open for it because it's for the betterment of the team and to improve the team and be a part of that new success that I believe is about to happen as well."

Whether or not he gets the call to join the team's coaching staff, Revis still makes his presence felt around the Jets. He recently attended New York's Nov. 1 game against the Las Vegas Raiders, partnering with American Express for the 2026 Shop Small activation at MetLife Stadium. The event spotlighted several local NYC-area small businesses as part of a tailgate pop-up, allowing fans to discover their unique offerings and engage with the business owners directly ahead of Small Business Saturday on Nov. 28.

"It's great to team up with Amex, they do a lot in the community for their clients. I think it was great, I was excited to be back in the area to support the team. ... I think small businesses are very vital and important to a local community," Revis said. "They bring people together. You build friendships, you build networks through those communities with small businesses. And I find it very exciting; that pop-up was very enlightening to see some of the creativity that some of these owners have with small businesses."

In Revis' eight seasons in New York, he experienced the success of back-to-back AFC Championship Game appearances in 2009 and 2010, as well as tough rebuild years that the current team is facing. As the Jets try to close out what will likely be a 16th straight year without a playoff appearance, Revis had advice for how Glenn and the players should approach the rest of this season.

"Aaron, as a player, he was a super competitor. I'm sure, as a coach, he is as well. I just would say to be optimistic," he said. "It's so tough to win on a Sunday, it really is. ... But I believe if you pay attention to the details of critiquing yourself as a head coach: What can I improve on? Where are my strengths? Where are my weaknesses? Where can I find a middle ground? And I think if he can do that on a week-to-week basis for the rest of the season, you can see more improvement in the team as well, because obviously he's the head coach, he's leading those guys. And maybe when you critique yourself that way, maybe you can get a couple more wins before the season is over, going into the offseason."

He added: "As a player, it can be frustrating for those guys, especially a guy like Garrett Wilson, whose track record is usually winning more games than losing. ... I know he wants to win now, and it can be frustrating that all the pieces are not falling into place. We paid him a ton of money, we have a lot of belief in his potential and his future. So, he will be a big part of our success in the near future as well. Once we can get a great quarterback in the draft, they can gel together and have that chemistry."

Despite the new incoming quarterback next year, Revis advocated for the Jets to hold on to veteran starter Geno Smith next season to ease the transition for the youngster.

"Love, love, love Geno as well. I think we need to bring Geno back. He's been playing well, even though the record doesn't show it, but his stats have been great. He doesn't turn over the ball a lot. He's a very smart quarterback. I think the new guy can come in and maybe sit, like [Fernando] Mendoza [with the Raiders]. Give the new quarterback some time to just get adjusted to the way of life of being a pro athlete," Revis said. "The players, I know it's frustrating, but show a lot of effort the rest of the games here in this season. Play hard, you're athletes, you know how to play the game. And see if you can squeeze in a couple wins going into the offseason, because that will rub off on you going into the new season."

As for the die-hard fans who stick with the Jets through all the highs and lows, Revis advised them to stay the course, pointing to the recent sports success in New York as a reason to be hopeful that brighter days are ahead for Gang Green.

"Man, I'll say this: the Knicks finally won. Obviously, it took 53 years. I think, right now, be patient. I know every week, we have such loyal fans. They wear the jerseys, they got man caves, they got it all. They come to support because they love the game and they want to win right now. I think that's great," he said. "I just think Darren Mougey, the GM, has done a great job with draft capital. I think we need to be excited for this upcoming draft, because there's no way that we're not going to pick a quarterback. We have to. There's so much college talent out there with these quarterbacks, and we should see who we pick.

"And I think whoever we pick, we should embrace it. We should embrace that. ... And we'll see. We'll just see. I'm very excited. And just be patient. I know this can be frustrating, but I think we should bring a lot of excitement into this new draft."

articles.title: Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker III ruled out for Week 10 matchup against Falcons with groin injury
articles.summary: Walker suffered the groin injury during Thursday's practice with the Chiefs.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons.

The NFL's second-leading rusher reported groin tightness on Friday morning and the team wants to "give him a week" to rest. Rookie running back Emmett Johnson will now handle first-team duties in Walker's absence.

Following Friday's practice, Chiefs head coach Andy Reid told reporters that the team wanted to see how Walker responded to treatment before making a final decision on his status for Week 10.

"We'll just see how he feels through this afternoon, with rehab and through tomorrow," Reid said. "Somewhere he tweaked it. We're kind of feeling it out just to see where we're at with that [groin]. We're not going to put him at risk. If he can go, he can go. If he can't, he can't."

Walker was listed as questionable on Friday's injury report .

In his first season with the Chiefs after signing a three-year, $43.05 million contract in March, Walker has 872 rushing yards and seven touchdowns through eight games. He is currently eight yards behind the NFL leader Bijan Robinson of the Falcons.

Johnson, the team's fifth-round pick in the 2026 draft out of Nebraska, has 111 rushing yards and a touchdown, plus 14 receptions for 237 and a touchdown this season. He has also served as the Chiefs' kick return man, picking up 318 return yards on 11 attempts.

Fantasy football impact of Walker's absence

Walker has not only helped carry the Chiefs offense but has also been one of fantasy football's best players over the season's first half. He has averaged 22.9 fantasy points per game in half-PPR scoring, second only to Jahmyr Gibbs among all running backs.

With Walker out, Johnson is a must-add in all fantasy leagues. At the time the news broke of Walker being ruled out, the rookie was available in 56% of Yahoo leagues. That number will skyrocket. Johnson has been one of the most valuable fantasy stashes all season for just such a situation. He has shown flashes in limited touches this season, including posting 22.8 fantasy points in Week 8 thanks to five receptions for 128 yards and a touchdown. He also found the end zone last week in a win over the Jets. Johnson will be a borderline fantasy RB1 in a matchup at Atlanta.

The Falcons have been lit up by RBs recently with injuries taking a toll, allowing Bucky Irving (170 total yards), Christian McCaffrey (RB6) and D'Andre Swift (RB5) to run wild. They also just traded away safety Jessie Bates this week. This sets up a potential big game with the Chiefs projected for 25.25 points as 3.5-point road favorites.

articles.title: New A.J. Brown, Rhamondre Stevenson Injury Updates Ahead of Patriots' Game vs. Lions in Germany
articles.summary: The New England Patriots have been riddled with injuries throughout the 2026 season, but two of their top offensive weapons may be available on Sunday, with running back Rhamondre Stevenson and wide receiver A.J. Brown both in contention to play, according to ESPN's Mike Reiss.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots have been riddled with injuries throughout the 2026 season, but two of their top offensive weapons may be available on Sunday, with running back Rhamondre Stevenson and wide receiver A.J. Brown both in contention to play, according to ESPN's Mike Reiss .

Stevenson suffered a knee injury during the team's loss to the Green Bay Packers last week. Early reports suggested that he could miss several weeks , but the running back has been "pushing to play."

Brown missed the past two games because of a knee issue, but he returned to practice this week. Vrabel felt "pretty good" about the wide receiver's status on Friday, per Reiss.

New England traded a 2028 first-round pick to acquire Brown from the Philadelphia Eagles in the offseason, and he was expected to serve as the top target for quarterback Drake Maye. So far, the results have been underwhelming.

Brown suffered an ankle injury in the regular-season opener and missed four games. He returned from the injured reserve in Week 6 and played against the New York Jets and Chicago Bears, but landed on the injury report with a knee issue after playing those two games in the span of four days.

The 29-year-old wide receiver has just nine receptions for 101 yards in three games this season.

Stevenson has arguably been New England's best offensive skill player this season. The sixth-year running back has 399 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 102 carries. He's also added 26 catches for 258 yards and two scores in the passing game. Stevenson leads the team with 657 yards from scrimmage.

New England can't afford to be without Stevenson, especially since running back TreVeyon Henderson was ruled out with an illness. Henderson has missed the past three games after being hospitalized with a medical emergency involving neurological symptoms, according to Mark Daniels of MassLive.

The Patriots have not lost back-to-back games under head coach Mike Vrabel, according to Reiss, but it won't be easy to keep that streak alive. New England will face the Detroit Lions on Sunday at the FC Bayern Stadium in Munich, Germany.

articles.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown Teases Germany Celebration vs. Patriots If He Scores 1st TD Since September
articles.summary: Detroit Lions star Amon-Ra St. Brown hopes to show off a German-themed touchdown celebration if he gets into the end zone during Sunday's game against the New England Patriots at Allianz Arena in Munich, Germany.
articles.body:
Detroit Lions star Amon-Ra St. Brown hopes to show off a German-themed touchdown celebration if he gets into the end zone during Sunday's game against the New England Patriots at Allianz Arena in Munich, Germany.

St. Brown, whose mother is from Germany, told reporters after Friday's practice he is working to figure out the proper celebration.

"I got to do something Germany related, with the culture, whether it's soccer," St. Brown said. "Anything German culture is what it's going to be. But exactly what I don't know yet. ... I don't have it planned yet. I got like two days to figure that out. I haven't been in the end zone in some weeks, so I feel like Germany would be a great time to touch the paint again."

Washington Commanders running back Craig Reynolds, who played with St. Brown in Detroit from 2021 to '25, told ESPN's Eric Woodyard the four-time Pro Bowler will regularly speak German when talking to his mom or brother:

"He speaks German to his mom all the time. Or he'll speak it to his brother if we're in public and they're trying to say something. But I don't like it because I don't know German. I feel like they're sneak dissing me when I'm around, so I don't like that s--t. "I've told him multiple times like, 'You can't be doing that when I'm around. Or you've got to tell me what you're saying or teach me what you're saying.' It's not fair for me to be in an elevator and you're talking to your brother in German while other people don't know what you're saying."

St. Brown holds dual citizenship between the United States and Germany. He also played for the German U19 football team in 2015 along with his brother, Osiris, that finished second at European Championships.

A touchdown on Sunday would also snap St. Brown's five-game drought. It's his longest streak without a touchdown since the 2022 season.

The Lions and Patriots will kickoff Sunday's NFL slate at 9:30 a.m. ET.

articles.title: Darian Mensah, Eagles GM Howie Roseman Meet in Viral Video at Miami Game After NFL Trade Deadline
articles.summary: Amid speculation about the Philadelphia Eagles potentially drafting a quarterback this year, general manager Howie Roseman fanned the flames.
articles.body:
Amid speculation about the Philadelphia Eagles potentially drafting a quarterback this year, general manager Howie Roseman fanned the flames.

Roseman made an appearance at Miami's matchup against Duke on Saturday and met up with quarterback Darian Mensah before the game.

Mensah is widely considered to be one of the top quarterbacks in this year's draft class, and it wouldn't be out of the realm of possibility for the Eagles to consider taking him if he's on the board.

articles.title: NFL Hall of Famer Fran Tarkenton has paid $51.89 million for a renovated five-bedroom Palm Beach mansion; the sellers had bought the property for $12.65 million in 2019 before overhauling its interiors
articles.summary: Former Minnesota Vikings quarterback Fran Tarkenton has bought a renovated five-bedroom mansion in Palm Beach, Florida, for a recorded $51.89 million,
articles.body: Former Minnesota Vikings quarterback Fran Tarkenton has bought a renovated five-bedroom mansion in Palm Beach, Florida, for a recorded $51.89 million, according to property records cited by Palm Beach Daily News. The 86-year-old Pro Football Hall of Famer purchased the Mediterranean-style residence at 1620 South Ocean Boulevard through the Tarkenton Revocable Trust. The sellers, Anthony and Lynda Lomangino, had acquired the property for $12.65 million in 2019 before undertaking an extensive renovation.The property is located on a stretch of South Ocean Boulevard known locally as Billionaires Row, a little over a mile south of US President Donald Trump's Mar-a-Lago Club. It sits on a corner lot measuring more than half an acre, across the road from the Atlantic Ocean, and comes with private beach access, according to its real estate listing. The two-storey Mediterranean-style home was built in 2006. Its sellers carried out a major overhaul, with the property described in the listing as having been rebuilt from the roof down. The renovation included a new roof, impact-resistant windows, updated landscaping, a generator and a new air-conditioning system.The interiors feature marble detailing, French wood-inlay flooring and pecky-cypress ceilings. The formal living room and a paneled library face the sea, while the second-floor primary bedroom suite also looks out towards the ocean. The suite includes a separate sitting room, two bathrooms and two closets. It also has a balcony with ocean views.The kitchen is fitted with a La Cornue stove and an island designed to seat 10 people. Other features include a card room, an elevator and a three-car garage. An open-air dining loggia with a fireplace overlooks a courtyard with a swimming pool and whirlpool spa. The property also has a newly built courtyard and landscaped outdoor spaces.The sales listing describes the house as offering more than 10,000 square feet of space. The property is spread across a lot of more than half an acre, with the ocean visible across South Ocean Boulevard. The mansion's location and private beach access were among the features highlighted in the marketing material.Tarkenton's agent, Jana Scarpa of Compass Florida, told Homes.com News that the former quarterback and his wife, Linda, had visited Palm Beach for years and were familiar with the area. She said she had a particular property in mind for them. Recalling their reaction when they entered the house, Scarpa said: "They walked in and said, 'Sold.'"Scarpa also represented the Lomanginos when they bought the property in 2019, making the latest transaction a return to a deal she had handled years earlier. According to Palm Beach Daily News, she said the sale brought the process "full circle" and that selling the property again was especially meaningful to her. She represented the buyers in the latest transaction, while Christian Angle of Christian Angle Real Estate was the listing broker.The mansion had been put on the market for $59 million, according to the listing broker's announcement. The recorded sale price of $51.89 million was therefore below the asking price. The difference between the Lomanginos' 2019 purchase price and the latest sale is substantial, although the renovation costs and other expenses associated with the property have not been publicly detailed. The gap between the two transaction prices should not be treated as the sellers' profit.For Tarkenton, the purchase comes decades after a career that made him one of the most recognisable quarterbacks of his generation. He began his NFL career with the Minnesota Vikings in 1961 and played for the franchise until 1966, before joining the New York Giants. He returned to Minnesota in 1972 and remained with the Vikings until retiring in 1978.Known for his ability to evade defenders and extend plays, Tarkenton helped lead the Vikings to three NFC championships. He was named the NFL's Most Valuable Player in 1975 and earned nine Pro Bowl selections during his career. At the time of his retirement, he held several major passing records, including career completions, passing yards and touchdown passes.Tarkenton was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1986. According to the Hall of Fame's records, he finished his career with 47,003 passing yards and 342 touchdown passes. After football, he worked in the computer-software industry, ran a business-consulting company and served as a commentator on *Monday Night Football* from 1979 to 1982.The Palm Beach purchase adds Tarkenton to the list of wealthy buyers drawn to the island's high-end property market. The Lomanginos, meanwhile, have also been active in the area's luxury real estate scene. Earlier in 2026, they paid a recorded $76.74 million for Villa Flora, a landmarked oceanfront mansion designed by architect Addison Mizner in 1923.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: NFL Insiders Doubt 'Colts Owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon Knows What She Wants in the Next GM'
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts are currently in a transitionary period, but even owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon may not know what the team's plans are just yet.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts are currently in a transitionary period, but even owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon may not know what the team's plans are just yet.

The Athletic's Jonathan Jones reported that insiders "did not get the impression" that Irsay-Gordon knows what she wants in the team's next general manager. Instead, the team is keeping its options open and improving its flexibility.

Irsay-Gordon relieved former general manager Chris Ballard of his duties in October. Interim general manager Ed Dodds spent the first few weeks of his new role trading away many of the team's best players ahead of the NFL's trade deadline last Tuesday.

The Colts moved on from wide receivers Keenan Allen and Josh Downs, guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner. The Colts were able to accumulate six draft picks for those four players, leaving them with 10 selections in the 2027 NFL Draft and eight selections in the 2028 NFL Draft.

Indianapolis does not have a 2027 first-round pick due to last year's acquisition of cornerback Sauce Gardner.

The moves also cleared up the team's finances, leaving Indianapolis with $33.8 million in available salary cap space, which is the fourth most in the league, according to Spotrac .

Indianapolis may not have a lot of talent on the roster, but Irsay-Gordon is making sure the next general manager has added resources to build a talented team.

articles.title: Donte Whitner calls for Jameis Winston’s release after Giants quarterback’s bizarre attempt to trick Washington Commanders
articles.summary: Former NFL safety Donte Whitner has strongly criticised New York Giants quarterback Jameis Winston and believes the team should release him after his
articles.body: Former NFL safety Donte Whitner has strongly criticised New York Giants quarterback Jameis Winston and believes the team should release him after his unusual attempt to distract the Washington Commanders during Thursday night’s game. Winston surprised everyone by singing the Baha Men’s hit song ‘Who Let the Dogs Out?’ while trying to draw Washington offside. However, his unusual approach failed, and Whitner was far from impressed.Donte Whitner wants the New York Giants to cut Jameis Winston after his Bizarre on-field anticsThe incident happened during the fourth quarter of the Giants’ 24-21 loss to the Washington Commanders on November 12. With New York facing a fourth-and-1 situation near its own end zone, Winston was brought in to try something different. The Giants wanted Washington’s defenders to move before the snap, which would have given them five free yards and another chance to keep possession.Winston first tried a different version of the usual quarterback count. He shouted, “Get ready, get set, hut one, hut two, hut three!” But when the Commanders refused to move, he took things in a completely different direction.The quarterback then started singing, “Who let the dogs out? Who, who, who?” referring to the popular song by the Baha Men.Unfortunately for Winston, the Washington defense did not fall for the trick. The Giants eventually had to punt, and the Commanders went on to win the game 24-21.While some viewers found the moment funny, former NFL safety Donte Whitner saw it very differently. Speaking on ESPN’s Get Up, he openly questioned Winston’s approach and said the quarterback was not taking the situation seriously enough.“I’d cut Jameis Winston this morning,” Whitner declared.He went on to explain why he felt the quarterback’s behaviour was unfair to his teammates, who were working hard to win the game.“It was so unrealistic. You have 10 other guys out there and guys on defense that are busting their butt every week, and it’s very hard and difficult to win a game in the National Football League,” Whitner said.The former NFL player also took issue with Winston’s traditional snap count before he started singing.“And then when you go into ‘Who Let the Dogs Out’? Are you serious? He’s clearly just trying to go viral on social media while they’re trying to win a football game. He’d get his pink slip this morning.”Whitner’s comments made it clear that he did not consider the moment harmless entertainment. For him, the bigger concern was that Winston appeared more interested in creating a memorable moment than helping his team.John Harbaugh defends Jameis Winston after Donte Whitner’s Giants criticismDespite Whitner’s strong reaction, Giants head coach John Harbaugh had a different view of Winston’s unusual approach. When reporters asked him about the incident on Friday, he made it clear that the quarterback had not come up with the idea during the game.Harbaugh explained that Winston had used similar calls throughout the season and that the singing was part of an attempt to confuse the defence.“No, it doesn’t bother me,” Harbaugh said when asked whether the incident concerned him.He added, “And that ‘Who Let the Dogs Out?’ thing, well it was, I think, probably, fun, on his part, so to speak. The way the cadence sounds, it was an attempt to still draw them offsides.”The coach also confirmed that he knew about the unusual cadence before the game. According to NBC Sports, Harbaugh had heard Winston use it during practice, so the move was not a surprise to him.Harbaugh’s explanation offered a different picture of the incident. While Whitner believed Winston was trying to attract attention, the Giants coach saw it as an attempt to gain an advantage against Washington’s defence.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: NFL Rule Changes for Onside Kicks Addressed by Insiders in New Rumors amid Concern Over 0 Recoveries
articles.summary: The NFL could "spend a lot of attention" on fixing the onside kick this offseason, The Athletic's Jonathan Jones reported.
articles.body:
The NFL could "spend a lot of attention" on fixing the onside kick this offseason, The Athletic's Jonathan Jones reported.

There have been zero recoveries on 22 onside-kick attempts through the first nine weeks of the 2026 season, which is the latest a season has gone without a single onside recovery since 2000, according to Jones.

The onside kick recovery rate was 19.5 percent between 2000 and 2017, per CBS Sports . That figure fell to 8.7 percent after 2018, when the league eliminated running starts. Since the new "dynamic kickoff" rules were introduced in 2024, onside kick recoveries have nearly gone extinct.

The league has tinkered with kickoffs for years, ranging from banning wedge blocks in 2009 to eliminating running starts entirely in 2018. In 2024, the NFL introduced the new " dynamic kickoff " with the intention of increasing kick returns and reducing injuries caused by high-speed collisions.

Under the new rules, teams were no longer allowed to attempt surprise onside kicks and could only declare an onside kick while they were trailing their opponent in the fourth quarter.

The league has attempted to modify those restrictions over the past two years, according to ESPN's Kevin Seifert . In 2025, the NFL allowed teams to declare an onside kick at any point rather than just the fourth quarter. This season, teams no longer needed to be trailing to declare an onside kick.

None of those small alterations have mattered. The league wants the recovery rate for onside kicks to be around 10 percent, according to Jones. To accomplish that, they'll likely have to tinker with the kickoff rules even more.

Jones reported that league executives have admitted that they focused more on fixing the kickoff return rate than fixing the onside kick, but "there's no way the surprise onside will come back."

articles.title: TreVeyon Henderson Put on IR by Patriots Amid Medical Condition, 'Unexplained Neurological Symptoms'
articles.summary: New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson will miss at least another month with the neurological issue that has sidelined him for two games.
articles.body:
New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson will miss at least another month with the neurological issue that has sidelined him for two games.

The Patriots announced Saturday Henderson has been placed on injured reserve ahead of Sunday's Week 10 matchup against the Detroit Lions in Munich, Germany.

Henderson last played in Week 7 during an Oct. 22 matchup at the Chicago Bears.

Week 10 Fantasy Injury Report and Last Minute Waiver Wire Replacements

He said in a Nov. 6 statement he had since experienced a "medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms that required hospitalization for several days."

The Patriots have a Week 11 bye. Henderson would be eligible for activation from IR at the earliest ahead of Week 15, during which the Patriots are slated for a Dec. 21 matchup at the Kansas City Chiefs.

Henderson said in his statement the neurological symptoms he was experiencing had "affected my strength, coordination, and some of my physical functions."

The running back also said medical testing provided "positive and reassuring" answers but had yet to reveal a cause for his symptoms.

"I am committed to doing everything necessary to return to full health," Henderson wrote. "My health and long-term well-being will remain my foremost priorities."

Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said Friday Henderson would not be traveling with his team to Munich.

"In terms of how he's doing, I talk to TreVeyon every day," Vrabel said. "And just like everybody else that's not available, he's working hard to get back, and when that is, I don't know. I don't have a timetable, but I love my interactions with him. I love talking with him and seeing how he's doing."

Henderson was coming off a 2025 rookie season in which he led the Patriots with 911 rushing yards and nine rushing touchdowns during the regular season, then saw his workload dip in favor of Rhamondre Stevenson on the Pats' way to Super Bowl LX.

The second-year back had recorded 203 rushing yards and one touchdown through six games of a season during which he was limited by a high ankle sprain before his most recent health issues.

Stevenson, who has led the Patriots with 399 rushing yards in nine games this season, was limited in practice this week with a knee injury. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Monday Stevenson "is expected to miss the next few weeks because of plantaris tendon issue in the back of his knee."

The Patriots did not activate a running back to the roster when placing Henderson on injured reserve Saturday, which the Boston Herald 's Doug Kyed noted could be a sign Henderson will be available Sunday.

As long as Stevenson is available, Vrabel is likely to continue looking for him to lead the Patriots' run game as Corey Kiner and Lan Larison provide backfield depth down this next stretch without Henderson.

articles.title: "I saw my mom go through....": Travis Kelce recalled mom Donna Kelce's inspiring career rise while raising two sons
articles.summary: Travis Kelce has spent years making headlines for his NFL achievements, but some of his most meaningful childhood memories have little to do with football.
articles.body: Travis Kelce has spent years making headlines for his NFL achievements, but some of his most meaningful childhood memories have little to do with football. The Kansas City Chiefs star recently offered a glimpse into the experiences that shaped him, recalling how he watched his mother, Donna Kelce, work her way towards professional success. What began as an occasional trip to her workplace after trouble at school became an early lesson in ambition, determination and the value of hard work. For Travis, those memories also explain why he holds his mother in such high regard.Travis Kelce recalls watching Donna Kelce climb the career ladderDuring an interview with British GQ published on August 12, 2025, Travis Kelce opened up about his childhood and the influence his parents had on his outlook. He remembered getting sent home from school after fighting and having to spend time at his mother's workplace.Those visits gave him a chance to see a side of Donna's life that he might otherwise have missed. She was not simply his mother managing family responsibilities. She was also a woman building a career and working towards goals of her own.Travis described how her position changed over the years as he continued visiting her office.“It went from cubicles to a really nice office in the back, to all of a sudden the offices are getting bigger and bigger and now she’s got her name on her office. I literally saw my mom go through it by being a little bad-ass kid.”..The memory carried a deeper meaning for the NFL star. He had witnessed his mother's progress without fully understanding what it took to achieve it. Looking back as an adult, he could recognise the determination behind those changes.Donna Kelce's career journey left a lasting impression on TravisDonna's professional journey was not without its challenges. She graduated with a communications degree from Ohio University in 1974 and initially hoped to build a career in radio or television. However, opportunities for women in those industries were limited at the time.Speaking about those barriers, Donna explained that the industries “would put up with [women] but didn’t see us as anything serious.”She eventually moved into banking and built a long career at KeyBank in Cleveland. Her progress from an entry-level position to a senior role became something her son admired.Travis also made it clear that his parents' influence extended beyond their professional lives. He credited both Donna and his father, Ed Kelce, with working hard to give him and his older brother, Jason Kelce, opportunities to pursue their ambitions.The story also offers a different perspective on Donna, who became widely recognised as the mother of two NFL stars. Long before the cameras followed her to football stadiums, she was building a career while raising two sons.For Travis, those childhood visits were more than an unexpected consequence of getting into trouble at school. They gave him a front-row seat to his mother's determination, something he continues to admire years later.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Travis Kelce-backed $200 million Six Flags could lose more than regional parks as financial pressure reaches new heights
articles.summary: Travis Kelce has built a reputation far beyond the football field, with investments and business partnerships expanding his portfolio.
articles.body: Travis Kelce has built a reputation far beyond the football field, with investments and business partnerships expanding his portfolio. But one of his entertainment ventures now sits in an industry facing financial uncertainty. Six Flags is struggling with nearly $5 billion in debt, and the possibility of selling some of its most famous amusement parks has raised fresh questions about the company's future. For Kelce, who has served as a Six Flags ambassador and investor, the financial pressure puts an interesting spotlight on one of his business interests.Travis Kelce’s Six Flags investment goes beyond a celebrity partnershipTravis Kelce's connection to Six Flags began before the company named him its ambassador. On October 21, 2025, he joined activist investment firm Jana Partners and executives Glenn Murphy and Dave Habiger in an investment group that acquired an approximately 9% economic interest in Six Flags. The group intended to work with management to improve shareholder value and the guest experience. However, the individual size of Kelce's investment was not disclosed.The NFL star later became the company's official brand ambassador in March 2026. The partnership gave Six Flags access to his popularity through social media campaigns, promotional appearances and marketing across its North American parks.His childhood connection to amusement parks also made the partnership a natural fit. Kelce said, "Six Flags parks were a hallmark of my childhood and the scene of some of my most fun and cherished memories, and I’m excited to team up with the company as it enters its next chapter."That next chapter, however, now comes with serious financial challenges.Six Flags debt crisis puts Cedar Point and Kings Island under scrutinySix Flags reported nearly $4.92 billion in total debt and $4.66 billion in net debt as of September 27, 2026. Its third-quarter revenue also fell 11% year over year to $1.17 billion. Although the company has reduced its debt by approximately $275 million since the end of 2025, the remaining burden is substantial.The company has already sold seven regional parks in a $331.4 million transaction. Now, management is examining other properties and real estate as it looks for ways to strengthen its finances. CEO John Reilly has described "optimizing the portfolio" as an important part of that effort.Cedar Point and Kings Island have emerged as possible sale candidates in industry discussions. Neither park has been officially named as a sale target, though. Finding buyers would also be difficult because major amusement parks require huge investments, specialist management and long-term operating commitments.California's Great America is also preparing for its final season in 2027 after Six Flags decided against extending its lease.For Kelce, the situation creates an interesting business storyline beyond his NFL career. His investment group originally backed the company with hopes of improving its value. Now, the challenge is helping a major entertainment brand navigate debt, park closures and difficult decisions about its future.Whether Six Flags can restore its financial strength without selling its biggest attractions remains an important question for investors and theme park fans alike.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Joe Burrow receives unexpected NFL recognition before Steelers game after achieving something only one quarterback has done better
articles.summary: Joe Burrow has given the Cincinnati Bengals plenty of reasons to believe in their playoff chances, and the NFL has now highlighted just how remarkable his
articles.body: Joe Burrow has given the Cincinnati Bengals plenty of reasons to believe in their playoff chances, and the NFL has now highlighted just how remarkable his recent performances have been. Ahead of Sunday's important clash with the Pittsburgh Steelers, the league announced a historic achievement for the quarterback. With both AFC North rivals entering Week 10 at 6-2, Burrow has another opportunity to turn his impressive run into a statement victory at Paycor Stadium.NFL highlights Joe Burrow's historic touchdown streak before Steelers gameThe NFL recognised Burrow's remarkable scoring run on November 14, revealing that the Bengals quarterback has recorded at least four combined passing and rushing touchdowns in four consecutive games. According to the league, that streak ranks second-longest since the 1970 merger.It is another major achievement for a quarterback who has been central to Cincinnati's four-game winning run. The Bengals have scored at least 30 points in each of those victories, showing how dangerous their offence has become heading into the division showdown.Burrow's individual numbers also explain why he has entered the MVP conversation. Through eight games, he has completed 74% of his passes for 2,386 yards, 23 touchdowns and six interceptions. His completion percentage leads the league, while his touchdown total sits at the top of the NFL rankings.The Steelers will have a difficult task containing him, particularly with Cincinnati playing at home. However, Pittsburgh has already beaten the Bengals once this season, giving Sunday's rematch added importance.Burrow made no attempt to downplay what is at stake.“Home field advantage in the playoffs is so important. This is as big of a game as we've had here for awhile,” Burrow said. “We lost to them earlier in the season, so number one with the standings at the end of the year you want that to be split and number two for first place outright”Bengals receive injury setbacks before Joe Burrow's Steelers showdownWhile Burrow's form offers encouragement, Cincinnati will have to manage several absences. Cornerback Jalen Davis, wide receiver Andrei Iosivas and guard Brian Parker II were not activated from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's game. All three were ruled out.Iosivas had made progress during the week, but the coaching staff reportedly wants him to complete a full week of practice before returning to action.There was also news from Pittsburgh. Tight end Pat Freiermuth was added to the Steelers' injury report with an illness and listed as questionable.Separately, the NFL announced a $23,882 fine for Atlanta Falcons receiver Drake London following an unnecessary roughness violation involving the use of his helmet against Bengals cornerback DJ Turner.With first place in the AFC North at stake, Cincinnati will need Burrow to maintain his exceptional form. A victory would also strengthen the Bengals' position in the race for a favourable playoff spot.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Keyshawn Johnson Says Deion Sanders Called Him over Comments About Shedeur in New Video
articles.summary: Former NFL wide receiver Keyshawn Johnson revealed that Colorado head coach Deion Sanders contacted him regarding comments made about his son, Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders.
articles.body:
Former NFL wide receiver Keyshawn Johnson revealed that Colorado head coach Deion Sanders contacted him regarding comments made about his son, Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders.

"I want to see Shedeur start," Johnson said during a recent appearance on ALL THE SMOKE: Unplugged (2:10 mark). "I want to see you start, Shedeur. I just want to make sure, because the last time I said something about him on TV he went and told his daddy. Then Prime had to call me and tell me to cuss his ass out."

"Prime was mad at me for that," he added. "Because he's just a kid, man. He didn't know. He thought I was saying something negative about him."

The exact remarks that Johnson made to elicit the response from Deion are uncertain, although he previously discussed the positives and negatives of Shedeur's rookie season in which he threw for 1,400 yards and seven touchdowns compared to 10 interceptions.

The younger Sanders entered the 2026 season as Cleveland's backup quarterback behind Deshaun Watson, but started his first game of the year during the Browns' 23-22 loss to the New Orleans Saints on Sunday.

Shedeur performed admirably despite the defeat, finishing 19-of-31 for 297 yards and two touchdowns without getting picked off.

articles.title: Who is Jahmyr Gibbs' girlfriend Nicole Anderson? Meet the model who refuses to use the NFL star's fame to grow her career
articles.summary: Being in a relationship with an NFL star can bring instant attention, but Nicole Anderson has chosen a different path.
articles.body: Being in a relationship with an NFL star can bring instant attention, but Nicole Anderson has chosen a different path. The girlfriend of Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs has built her own identity through modelling, content creation and real estate. While she regularly supports Gibbs during his football journey, Anderson has made it clear that she does not want his celebrity status to define her career. Her approach offers a different look at life alongside one of the NFL's rising stars.Nicole Anderson builds her career beyond Jahmyr Gibbs' NFL spotlightAnderson has developed a growing presence in the fashion and digital entertainment world. Represented by The INDUSTRY Model Management, she has worked with brands including New Era, Tangle Teezer and Victoria's Secret.Her social media platforms have also attracted a substantial audience, with approximately 178,000 Instagram followers and nearly 248,000 TikTok followers at the time of the original report. Her content ranges from fashion inspiration and beauty routines to travel experiences.However, Anderson has been careful about how she presents her relationship online. In an October 2025 interview with People, she explained why she avoids using Gibbs' football career to attract followers.“I didn’t really want it to be something where I didn’t just enjoy making videos,” she told the outlet. “I post because I actually enjoy doing it. So that’s why I also have my real estate license.”She also told People, “When I do make my videos, I don’t say like, ‘Get ready with me like for my boyfriend’s game,’” she told People in October 2025. “I don’t try and use his name as a ‘Follow me.’”Jahmyr Gibbs' girlfriend Nicole Anderson balances modelling and real estateContent creation is only one part of Anderson's professional life. She has also established herself in real estate, holding licences in Illinois and Michigan.Her interest in the property business began much earlier. Watching HGTV shows such as House Hunters, Love It or List It and Property Brothers with her mother helped spark her interest. That childhood curiosity eventually developed into a professional career.According to her Crain Homes biography, she now focuses on helping clients find their dream homes. The company also serves as the official luxury real estate partner of the Detroit Lions.Away from work, Anderson and Gibbs have been together since 2023. They have also developed a reputation for creative Halloween costumes, including their Spider-Man and Gwen Stacy outfits in 2025.Anderson has spoken warmly about their relationship, telling SI Lifestyle, “He always makes everything fun,” Anderson gushed about Gibbs to SI Lifestyle in 2025. “He’s just silly all the time, just crazy, and he can make anything fun.”For Anderson, supporting Gibbs and building an independent career are not competing priorities. She appears determined to make room for both.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Luke Fahey takes step forward in Ohio State football's win over Northwestern
articles.summary: A fourth-down touchdown pass highlighted the growth of freshman quarterback Luke Fahey as Ohio State snapped a two-game skid against Northwestern.
articles.body:
Luke Fahey rolled out of the pocket as Ohio State clung to a one-point lead.

It was fourth down late in the third quarter, and the Buckeyes needed only a yard to move the chains against Northwestern, but they didn't attempt to barrel through the line of scrimmage behind six offensive linemen.

The Buckeyes instead put their trust in the freshman quarterback .

As Fahey moved to his left, he found wide receiver Devin McCuin, who had slipped open underneath the coverage and brought in the pass for an 8-yard touchdown.

The score not only cushioned the Buckeyes' lead in a 28-19 triumph over Northwestern on Nov. 14 that snapped their two-game skid, but it also marked a step forward for Fahey.

Fahey had underthrown a pass to McCuin on a similar fourth-down attempt in the previous week's loss to Oregon, a turnover on downs in the middle of the Buckeyes' spiral against the Ducks.

"It was definitely good knowing that we had an opportunity to take that sprintout last week," Fahey said. "I missed it. Unfortunately, that was on me."

OSU Buckeyes face Northwestern in college football matchup. See the photos

His latest pass found McCuin, who shed a potential tackle by cornerback Ore Adeyi near the goal line and dove inside the pylon for the score.

"That's the growth of a young quarterback," coach Ryan Day said.

The Buckeyes could have taken three points, but Day resisted settling for a field goal after they had exhausted nearly seven minutes of game clock to reach the doorstep of the end zone. He wanted seven points.

When the Buckeyes called for a timeout before going for it on fourth down, they dialed up the pass.

"It's been a little bit of a mixed bag on the move for him," Day said, "but you can't crawl up into a ball in those moments. If we had the right look, we were going to run it. If not, we decided to pass it. It's a play that we all have been working on.

"The guys knew what it was, and it was the time to call it, but you've got to go put it on the field."

As Fahey made his third start in place of the injured Julian Sayin , he threw for 201 yards and three touchdowns.

Fahey wasn't without blemishes. He threw an interception on Ohio State's opening drive when his pass bounced off the helmet of Chris Henry Jr. and landed in the hands of cornerback Braden Turner. He was off target on a handful of throws while rolling right.

But Fahey positioned the Buckeyes for a win by peppering passes to star wide receiver Jeremiah Smith from the get go.

Smith, who had 11 catches for 117 yards and one touchdown, accounted for more than half of Fahey's passing yards.

"I definitely think the chemistry is coming along a lot more," Fahey said. "I'm being able to talk to him a lot more, getting more reps with him. He's a great player with a great attitude. It certainly makes my job easy to target him and get him the ball."

Luke Fahey in action: Photos from 2026 Ohio State football season

Fahey completed a series of critical late passes as well. He helped to seal the win in the fourth quarter when he flung a pass over the middle to Smith for a 10-yard touchdown.

The throw came in the face of a heavy pass rush as Fahey squeezed the ball between two defenders.

It left him with a long-anticipated milestone.

Fahey, who grew up in Southern California rooting for Ohio State , had led the Buckeyes to his first win behind center.

"It's truly unreal," he said, "to kind of be playing the game and then finally get a win, words can't describe how I feel right now."

Joey Kaufman covers Ohio State football for The Columbus Dispatch. Email him at jkaufman@dispatch.com and follow him on @joeyrkaufman on X.

articles.title: Commanders’ ‘Biggest Disappointment’ Becoming Breakout Star
articles.summary: Commanders' 'Biggest Disappointment' becoming breakout star after win over Giants. The post Commanders’ ‘Biggest Disappointment’ Becoming Breakout Star appea...
articles.body:
It seemed like the Washington Commanders did everything they could, since drafting tight end Ben Sinnott in the 2nd round of the 2024 NFL Draft, to make sure he wouldn't have an NFL career.

Sinnott, a constant afterthought from the moment he got on the roster, was forced into action in Week 9 against the New York Giants after an injury to starter Chigo Okonkwo and delivered big in a 24-21 win.

Sinnott had 4 receptions for 42 yards and 1 touchdown on 4 targets in what was essentially a must-win game for the Commanders, who improved to 3-5-1 and stayed in the hunt for a playoff bid.

So the question now is … will the Commanders keep going with Sinnott?

"Sinnott can be most effective in the middle of the field, more so than out on the perimeter," Commanders Wire's Ivan Lambert wrote on November 14. "He can do real damage when his shoulders are square, and he is running hard forward, not side to side. After last night, many of us are now hoping OC David Blough and QB Jayden Daniels will want to go back to Sinnott more often."

articles.title: NFL Announces Twist for Steelers-Bengals Week 10 Matchup
articles.summary: ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Saturday backup Don Willard will work as the referee for the Pittsburgh Steelers-Cincinnati Bengals Week 10 matchup Sunday nigh...
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers will still fly to Ohio to face the Cincinnati Bengals for their Sunday night affair in Week 10. But the matchup will have a different referee than originally planned.

The league announced side judge Don Willard will serve as the referee for the AFC North clash because of the ground stop that halted flights for hours to begin the weekend.

Willard will be able to get to Cincinnati without air travel. The Steelers-Bengals game will be one of four NFL matchups with a backup referee during Week 10.

ESPN's Adam Schefter posted the announcement from the league on his X account Saturday:

"Due to the ongoing nationwide impact to air travel this weekend, the NFL has adjusted its officiating assignments for Week 10 games, reassigning officials to games within driving distance of their hometowns," the statement read .

"The changes will necessitate that three back up referees — umpires Barry Anderson and Duane Heydt and side judge Don Willard — will work as referees."

Steelers-Bengals Get New Referee in Week 10

The Carolina Panthers-New Orleans Saints, Jacksonville Jaguars-Tennessee Titans and Miami Dolphins-Indianapolis Colts are the other matchups that will have different referees Sunday because of the air travel chaos around the country this weekend.

"Each of the league's 17 officiating crews have a backup referee identified, and that individual trains throughout the year to work at the referee position should the need arise," the statement concluded .

The NFL had Clete Blakeman originally scheduled to be the referee for the Steelers-Bengals matchup Sunday.

It's difficult to judge how this change might impact the Steelers-Bengals matchup. Blakeman and his crew entered Week 10, though, with the fourth-most penalties in the league this season. So, perhaps without Blakeman, there will be fewer fouls called Sunday night.

But the rest of the officiating crew besides Blakeman will remain the same. It's that crew that sits ranked fourth in the league with the most fouls called per game.
